title: Covering Indexes and Read-Query Design
learningObjectives: Define a covering index and explain how it can avoid table-row lookups.
Identify the columns a query needs for filtering and output.
Create a selective covering index for a read-heavy query.
Use EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN to identify USING COVERING INDEX.
Explain the storage and write-maintenance cost of wider indexes.

understand.concept: A covering index contains all columns needed by a query's search conditions and selected output. The engine may be able to answer the query from the index without looking up the table row, reducing additional table access.
understand.whyItMatters: Covering indexes can improve read-heavy workloads, but wider indexes use more storage and increase write costs.
understand.analogy: An index is like a sorted lookup guide that points toward the relevant records instead of requiring every page to be read.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not model B-tree pages, query planner estimates, index maintenance or the full range of SQL access paths.

explain.narrative:
## Covering index concept
An index can cover a query when it contains the columns used by the query's filters and output. SQLite may report USING COVERING INDEX in EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN when it can satisfy the query from the index alone.

## Design trade-offs
Adding output columns to an index can make it wider. Wider indexes consume more pages and increase maintenance work. Use covering indexes selectively for frequent, measured queries.

## Verify the plan
Use EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN to confirm whether the index is covering for the specific query. A change to the SELECT list or WHERE clause can change whether the index covers the query.

examples.title: Create a customer payment table
examples.code: CREATE TABLE perf15_payments (payment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer TEXT NOT NULL, payment_status TEXT NOT NULL, amount INTEGER NOT NULL, note TEXT);
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create a customer payment table in SQLite. Verify both the access strategy and the returned data.

examples.explanation: This example demonstrates insert sample payments in SQLite. Verify both the access strategy and the returned data.

examples.title: Create an index that covers a frequent report
examples.code: CREATE INDEX idx_perf15_cover ON perf15_payments(customer, payment_status, amount);
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create an index that covers a frequent report in SQLite. Verify both the access strategy and the returned data.

examples.title: Inspect the covering-index plan
examples.code: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT amount FROM perf15_payments WHERE customer = 'Asha' AND payment_status = 'paid';
examples.expectedOutput: Query plan uses a covering index
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates inspect the covering-index plan in SQLite. Verify both the access strategy and the returned data.

examples.code: SELECT amount FROM perf15_payments WHERE customer = 'Asha' AND payment_status = 'paid';
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates run the covered report query in SQLite. Verify both the access strategy and the returned data.

practise.guidedTask: Run the examples and identify which query columns are present in the covering index.
practise.independentTask: Choose a frequent report query from a sample table. Design a covering index, inspect its plan and explain why adding more columns may not always be beneficial.

questions.prompt: What can USING COVERING INDEX indicate?
options: The query can be answered from the index without an extra table lookup
questions.answer: The query can be answered from the index without an extra table lookup
questions.explanation: The plan detail identifies an index that covers the query.

questions.prompt: Which columns should a covering index include?
options: The columns needed for filtering and selected output
questions.answer: The columns needed for filtering and selected output
questions.explanation: A covering index should include the query's required search and result columns.

questions.prompt: What is a downside of wider covering indexes?
questions.explanation: Wider indexes consume more pages and require more update work.

questions.prompt: When should a covering index be added?
options: When measured read patterns justify its cost
Only when a table has one row
Whenever a column is named id
questions.answer: When measured read patterns justify its cost
questions.explanation: Index design should be based on measured workload needs.
